clue.text: After leave, order for combatant, perhaps, reversed

parts.note: a soldier who has had leave and returned is back
'To the front!' is a command a soldier might be given

explanation.surface: A soldier's orders after leave come out the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: The military surface dresses both halves: a soldier comes BACK after leave, and TO FRONT is the order sending a combatant forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Something turned round with its rear foremost has been reversed in direction.

clue.text: Seafront?

parts.note: not the promenade but the front end of a seagoing vessel

explanation.definitionFit: The forward part of a ship is the front of a craft at sea.

clue.text: Windsor doctor, lacking the craft of 11 ac

indicators.note: lacking says the letters for the craft are removed

parts.note: the answer to 11 across, the conspirator
SS stands for steamship, a craft

explanation.surface: A doctor in Windsor without a ship's skill.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Caius is the French physician in Shakespeare's The Merry Wives of Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic French physician in a Shakespeare comedy set in the royal town.

clue.text: Pound I contributed separately to voucher for author

indicators.note: contributed means the letter I is put into the developing voucher word as well
separately to says the pound letter goes into the voucher at its own spot, apart from the I

parts.note: a token is a voucher, like a book token
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: Someone puts a pound into a book voucher to buy a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes after TO and I after K, giving TO-L-K-I-EN.
explanation.definitionFit: The writer of The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings.

clue.text: Anticipate everyone supporting football team

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting word sits below the other

parts.note: Nottingham Forest is an English football club, known simply as Forest
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Every fan backs the local team, predicting a win.
explanation.definitionFit: To act in advance to prevent or pre-empt something.

clue.text: Formerly nameless, an enormous expanse

indicators.note: nameless asks us to remove N, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: once means formerly
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vast, once unnamed region.
explanation.walkthrough: N is a standard abbreviation for name; ONCE without it is OCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge body of sea water is a vast stretch.

clue.text: Like the Vicar of Bray, after visit to barber?

explanation.surface: A turncoat cleric goes for a haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: The Vicar of Bray, in the old song, switched faith with each monarch to keep his living: a trimmer is such a time-server.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who changes sides for advantage; and neater after a haircut.

clue.text: Parties brought back to earth

indicators.note: brought back says the word for parties is read from right to left

parts.note: dos is an informal word for parties or celebrations

explanation.surface: Revellers are brought down to earth after the celebrations.
explanation.definitionFit: A clod of turf or soil is a synonym for earth in the gardener's sense.

clue.text: Told to look carefully over luggage for flight

indicators.note: told means the words are spoken, so we go by how they sound

parts.note: stare means look carefully and a case is luggage

explanation.surface: A traveller is told to check their bags before boarding a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests air travel; it means a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of steps between floors is called a flight of stairs.

clue.text: Die consoled, converted, and having given up one's possessions

indicators.note: converted says the letters are changed into a new form

explanation.surface: A dying person, comforted and converted, gives everything away.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation that has granted independence to its colonies.

clue.text: Absolutely plain water girl's drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling into a new arrangement

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A girl has had too much water, which is perfectly obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absolutely plain' reads as an adjective phrase, and so does the answer: written large means obvious, writ being the old past participle.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase for something shown on a large scale, so obvious nobody could miss it.

clue.text: Sarah's son is ecstatic, finally getting a double first

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a double first is a degree with top class twice, so the letter for a top grade appears twice
finally takes the closing letter of ecstatic

explanation.surface: A mother is overjoyed when her son earns top honours twice.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, Sarah bore Isaac in old age and laughed, which suits 'ecstatic'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible the patriarch Abraham's wife bore him one child, the boy named in Genesis 21.

clue.text: Conspirator putting radioactive element into liqueur

indicators.note: putting one thing into another tells us to place the element inside the liqueur

parts.note: cassis is a blackcurrant liqueur
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A plotter spikes someone's drink with something radioactive.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the plotters who killed Julius Caesar, famous for his lean and hungry look.

clue.text: All one has left, after parting with cheque?

definitions.text: All one has left, after parting with cheque?

parts.words: All one has left, after parting with cheque?
parts.note: the stub retained in a chequebook after the cheque itself is torn off and handed over

explanation.definitionFit: The retained stub of a cheque or ticket kept as a record.

clue.text: For example, one in millions finding surroundings strangely unreal

indicators.note: finding surroundings says the M acquires letters wrapped around it
strangely says the letters of unreal are rearranged

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: Someone who is one in a million finds their surroundings oddly dreamlike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' turns UNREAL into NUERAL, and M goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure 1 is a written symbol for a number, as are 2, 3 and so on.

clue.text: Pope not involved with pastoral activity?

explanation.surface: A pontiff who stays clear of country pursuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pastoral' tempts toward a priest's flock; here it means the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Several popes took this name; it also means of the town rather than the country.

clue.text: In North Africa, it's dreadful behaviour

indicators.note: In says the following word sits inside the region's name

parts.note: Barbary is the old name for the coastal region of North Africa
the possessive adds no letter; it's gives it

explanation.surface: Something terrible happening along the North African coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Savage cruelty or brutal, uncivilised conduct.

clue.text: Roman coin, particular find

parts.note: the as was a small bronze coin of ancient Rome
certain means particular, as in 'a certain person'

explanation.surface: An archaeologist turns up a specific Roman coin.
explanation.definitionFit: To find out or establish something for sure is a verb synonym.

clue.text: No verdict could be arranged

indicators.note: could be says the letters may become something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: A jury fails to reach a decision on how things were settled.
explanation.definitionFit: Devised or contrived, worked out artificially.

clue.text: Waterproof material physicist immersed in lake

indicators.note: immersed in places the physicist inside the word for lake

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake
Wolfgang Pauli was the Austrian physicist of the exclusion principle

explanation.surface: A scientist dunked in a lake wishes he had brought a waterproof.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy canvas proofed against rain, used as a protective covering sheet.

clue.text: Section of trail men tackled could be cold

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Walkers on a stretch of path tackle the risk of a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: A common cold is one example of an illness.

clue.text: Cavalry regiment's horses

explanation.surface: Describing the mounts of a mounted regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Scots Greys were a famous British cavalry regiment; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey-coated horses are commonly called by this plural, and the Scots regiment rode them.

clue.text: With outrageous interruption, presented dance

indicators.note: interruption says the letters break into the middle of the other word

parts.note: gave means presented, as a gift
OTT stands for over the top, meaning outrageous

explanation.surface: A performance of a dance is disrupted outrageously.
explanation.definitionFit: A French court dance of the 17th and 18th centuries.

clue.text: Substantial fortune put into new shares

parts.note: real means substantial or actual
lot means fortune or fate

explanation.surface: A large fortune is reinvested in fresh stock.
explanation.definitionFit: To allocate again, dividing something into a fresh set of portions.

clue.text: Bones of primate identified without hesitation

indicators.note: without says the hesitation sound is taken out

parts.note: a tarsier is a small large-eyed primate of Southeast Asia
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Bones from a primate are identified straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: The small bones of the ankle, the plural of tarsus.

clue.text: Prepared for exams to be corrected

explanation.surface: A student swots and fixes the mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A student goes over the material before a test; a text is amended after errors are found.

clue.text: Second try to remove warm coat

parts.note: to hear a case is to try it in court

explanation.surface: Someone takes a second go at getting their coat off.
explanation.definitionFit: To clip the fleece from a sheep, removing its woolly covering.

clue.text: Sheepish opening of Bacchic ode?

explanation.surface: A shy poet starts a hymn to the god of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer into O VINE, the natural apostrophe that might open a poem to Bacchus, god of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to sheep; and a poet hailing the grape would begin with the vocative 'O'.

clue.text: Sappers taking spades from gear used in services to make fortification

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are called sappers

indicators.note: taking spades from means the S is removed from the word for church gear

parts.note: a vestment is a garment worn by clergy at church services
S is the card-game abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: Army engineers borrow spades from church robes to build a defence.
explanation.definitionFit: A retaining wall or facing of stone that supports a rampart or embankment.

clue.text: Slur on score in match

explanation.surface: A smear on the scoreline during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: In music a slur and a tie are similar curved marks on a score; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved line joining notes in music; and a cup fixture or an equal result.

clue.text: Remained out of order

explanation.surface: Something stayed put because it was broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' suggests broken; here it means not in holy orders, not clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of lie, as in stayed lying; and non-clerical, outside the ordained.

clue.text: Poor class's academic achievement in rigorous examination

explanation.surface: A weak student's result from a tough exam.
explanation.walkthrough: A third is the lowest British honours degree class; the phrase also means harsh police questioning.
explanation.definitionFit: A lowly university classification, and also an intense interrogation by police.
